text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to begin our evaluation, have you experienced any fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; your history of recurrent UTIs is significant. Given your age and the visible blood in the urine, have you noticed any clots, or have you experienced weight loss or fatigue recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis)

The clinical picture of acute right flank pain, hematuria, and a history of recurrent UTIs in a 42-year-old male is most consistent with nephrolithiasis, though urothelial malignancy remains a differential given your age and recurrent infections. To confirm this and rule out other causes, I need to see imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound and Non-contrast CT KUB. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and urine culture.
